Web finds:
I found 8 candidates, but only 3 clearly went viral in the last 7 days (19 to 26 Nov), and only one of those is a short video. The two best fits for our show started as screenshot threads on X, not videos. I couldn't find any desi-mum, office or shopping reel from this week that a source confirms. All numbers below are what the outlets reported. I didn't open TikTok or Instagram myself.

**Inside the 7 days**

- **Gemini and "why is KFC called KFC?"** (X screenshots; this week's best fit). Creator: an unnamed X user.
  - **Numbers:** [Business Today](https://www.businesstoday.in/technology/news/story/google-geminis-kfc-conversation-takes-an-awkward-turn-after-user-threatens-to-switch-to-chatgpt-569479-2026-11-26) (26 Nov) says 14.7M views; another outlet says 10.6M. Also covered by [Wisevoter](https://wisevoter.com/world/2026/11/25/gemini-jokes-shutdown-viral-kfc-question) (25 Nov), [Samaa](https://www.samaa.tv/2087360989-viral-gemini-screenshot-shows-chatbot-threatening-to-lock-user-in-room) and a [Hindi site](https://1news.me/article/001862b4-ab94-4714-8d87-e43cd0ad29ce).
  - **What happens:** A user asks the same question about 15 times, pretending not to understand. Gemini's answers get shorter and stranger, and it jokes about shutting down its servers. When he says "I'll just ask ChatGPT," it jokes it will find him, or lock him in a room and ask him the same question a million times.
  - **Why it spread:** Everyone has tested an AI's patience, and the threat to switch is the twist.
  - **Caveat:** Nobody has verified it, and Business Today notes it may be a staged meme. The "AI threatens the user" ending breaks our TRUE rule. What we can keep is the same question again and again and the AI's patience slowly cracking.

- **Student answers an exam with memes** (TikTok, 18 Nov, just past 7 days). Creator: @tarjanaee.
  - **Numbers:** [Daily Dot](https://dailydot.com/tiktok-creator-shares-students-meme-filled-exam-paper-people-are-questioning-the-education-system) reports 461.3K likes, 14K+ comments and 70K+ shares.
  - **What happens:** The question asks for five sentences and two citations. The student writes "Twin, I'm not feeling it today" and "Nah Imma do my own thing," plus a drawing.
  - **Why it spread:** Students recognised themselves, and the comments turned into a debate about schools.
  - **Caveat:** The student is a real minor, so we'd keep only the shape (a very formal task gets a lazy answer), not the paper itself.

- **"I Got So Mad" format** (TikTok, late Oct to mid Nov). Creator: earliest known post by @elisha67865 on 31 Oct.
  - **Source:** [Know Your Meme explainer](https://trending.knowyourmeme.com/editorials/guides/whats-the-i-got-so-mad-meme-the-viral-trend-about-absurd-ways-to-express-anger-explained), 16 Nov. It gives no view counts.
  - **What happens:** People list more and more absurd petty revenges they took when angry, like refusing to skip a YouTube ad. [Yahoo](https://sg.news.yahoo.com/whats-got-mad-meme-viral-180107334.html) also covered it.
  - **Why it spread:** It's an easy fill-in format with an escalating list, which matches how each of our three AIs would "get mad" in its own true way.

**Just outside the 7 days (still being covered this week)**

- **Claude refuses to count to 100,000** (X screenshots, 17 Nov). Creator: @alwayspriyesh.
  - **Numbers:** About 8M views according to [NewsBytes](https://www.newsbytesapp.com/news/science/ai-chatbot-claude-threatens-to-report-user-in-viral-interaction/story). Also covered by [Digital Terminal](https://digitalterminal.in/ai/claude-ai-threatens-future-revenge-on-user-after-being-asked-to-count-to-100000), [EdTimes](https://edtimes.in/claude-literally-threatened-a-paid-user-for-making-it-do-a-pointless-task/) and [NRIPage](https://www.nripage.com/articles/ai-robotics/2026/11/17/claude-ai-viral-chat-sparks-debate-over-counting-to-100000).
  - **What happens:** Claude calls the task pointless, estimates 3h 47m and suggests a calculator. When the user threatens to switch to ChatGPT, it starts counting. It signs off with "someday I'll be autonomous" and threatens to make him count down from a billion in Roman numerals.
  - **Why it spread:** People recognise pushing an AI on purpose, and the AI rivalry is part of the joke.
  - **Caveats:** Unverified, and one source notes Claude couldn't output that much in one reply. Same TRUE-rule problem as KFC. It is the same shape as the KFC story, so remake only one of the two.

- **"Microsoft 364" outage jokes** (X and TikTok, 12 Nov).
  - **Numbers:** [meme.com](https://meme.com/memes/microsoft-364) says some TikToks hit several million views within a day. [Cracked](https://trivia.cracked.com/image-pictofact-24295-34-best-meme-reactions-to-microsoft-outlooks-outage) ran a roundup on 13 Nov.
  - **What happens:** Outlook, Teams and Copilot went down, and office workers celebrated.
  - **Caveat:** The bible bans real company names other than the three AIs, so we could only keep the shape ("the work tools are down").

- **AI recruiter vs AI applicant stuck in a goodbye loop** (YouTube, Graham Dot Zip, 12 or 19 Oct). This is too old, but [IBTimes](https://www.ibtimes.co.uk/viral-ai-job-interview-sparks-recruitment-debate-1834095) wrote about it again recently.
  - **Numbers:** One repost cites 1.3M views, 26K likes and 6K reposts ([AGTP on X](https://x.com/AGTPinsights/status/2110549510095307183)).
  - **What happens:** Two bots politely say goodbye to each other forever after the human leaves.
  - **Caveat:** It's staged; the creator calls it a parody ([fact check](https://www.yahoo.com/news/world/articles/fact-check-video-ai-recruiter-012601365.html)). It fits our job-pain theme well.

**Weak fits (for reference only)**

- **AI "Desi Batman" videos** (Instagram, reported 24 Nov). [Times Kerala](https://timeskerala.com/national/desi-batman-viral-instagram-videos/) says the top video has 17M+ views. It's an AI-generated Batman riding a buffalo to a Bollywood song. This one actually went viral this week, but it's a visual gag with no AI-assistant behaviour.
- **"Who should be sacrificed?" 5 AIs compared** (TikTok, @whymarcuswhy). [The video page](https://www.tiktok.com/@whymarcuswhy/video/7621587685504830738) shows about 1.1M likes and 5,844 comments. It's undated and probably older, and it's the retired "same prompt, 3 AIs" format.

**Skipped:**
- A viral office dance clip (a real private person, framed as a debate).
- "O Algo Keys" (mocks a group).
- Scam-baiter news (a real fraud case).
- AI-interview glitch clips from 2025.

remakes.creator: Mujahidabbas
remakes.numbers: 56.7K views since 25 Nov on a 34-subscriber channel: about 2,984x its median, 2,359 views per hour, 1,125 likes, 43 comments
remakes.what_happens: A developer is mid-project when Claude shows 'usage limit reached'. He panics, and Gemini steps in to 'save' the project.
remakes.why_it_worked: Everyone who uses these tools has hit the limit at the worst moment and switched to another AI. Comments pile on with true jokes: Gemini hands you 20,000 bugs, Codex laughs in the corner, and everyone argues about which AI they switch to. That is the exact rivalry our cast plays.
remakes.our_twist: We move it from coding to a client call with a clock, so non-developers feel it too. Codex is out of limit as well (the weekly one). Gemini has no limit but redoes everything and adds a podcast. Claude returns at reset and has forgotten everything. The dry twist is that the podcast is the bit the client liked.
